lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Pluto, we simply cannot tolerate having this dog Menippus as a neighbor. Either move him somewhere else, or we are relocating to another neighborhood.
lines.description: formal complaint, grandly offended and utterly sincere

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What is he doing to you? He's dead, just like you.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we start wailing and groaning—remembering our lives up there, Midas here crying over his gold, Sardanapalus over his endless luxuries, and me over my treasures—he laughs at us. He insults us, calling us slaves and scum. Sometimes he actually sings to drown out our lamentations. He is a complete nuisance.
lines.description: building outrage, aggrieved tenant listing damages

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.description: tired sigh, already knows the answer

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Every word, Pluto. I despise them. They're pathetic, degenerate creatures. It wasn't enough for them to lead terrible lives; now they're dead, and they're still obsessing over the upper world. So yes, I enjoy annoying them.
lines.description: cheerfully candid, no shame at all

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: But you shouldn't. They're upset. They've lost a great deal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Are you losing your mind, Pluto? Siding with their whining?

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Not at all. I just want to keep the peace.
lines.description: flat, practical, no appetite for drama

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well, listen here, you absolute dregs of Lydia, Phrygia, and Assyria: I am never going to stop. Wherever you move, I will follow you. I will annoy you, I will sing over you, and I will laugh at you.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. The outrage was what you did while you were alive—demanding that people bow down to you, trampling on free men, entirely forgetting that death existed. So go ahead and weep. You've been stripped of all of it.
lines.description: calmly cutting, factual rather than moralizing

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: [crying] Oh gods, my vast, magnificent estates...

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: [laughs] Excellent, keep it up. You wail, and I'll chant 'Know Thyself' on a loop. It makes the perfect backing track for this sort of whining.
lines.description: delighted, dry punchline with musical mischief
